newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX in talks with London oil exchange on linkups.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX in talks with London oil exchange on linkups.

text.p: The New York Mercantile Exchange is in talks with London's International Petroleum Exchange about a joint electronic trading system and other links aimed at lowering the cost of doing business.
However, the two exchanges are not contemplating a full-blown merger, NYMEX President Patrick Thompson said.
"There are two areas we think would be of immediate interest to our two customers," he said Monday.

Thompson said the exchanges were mulling joining contracts through electronic trading systems and revising margins to reduce the amount of cash traders have to pay up front when they simultaneously trade on both exchanges.
He said that he expected to make an announcement on the linkups later in the week.
"It's all a bit premature. We have to talk much further before we can talk about done deals or anything else," he said.

"System-wise, regulatory-wise we need to look into what the implications are and whether we can support those things. I think those are things that can be ironed out but they do take a lot of that fine print that goes into such a deal."

As well as benefits for the two exchanges' members, Thompson said the talks were also spurred by concern that after years of rapid growth, volumes in crude and oil product futures had been trailing off in recent years.
The average monthly trading volumes on the NYMEX crude oil futures market averaged 1.91 million contracts last year after peaking at more than 2 million per month in 1993 and 1994.
By comparison, the 1980s saw huge growth, with volumes jumping to 1.98 million in 1990 from 690,000 in 1986.
London's IPE Brent crude oil contract grew rapidly in the 1990s but has also flattened out since 1994.
Despite the areas of common interest, Thompson said the two exchanges wanted to remain independent.
"Both of us intend to retain our independence as institutions long after this -- a merger is not even on the table," he said.
